description.narrative:
“Reducing vulnerability in Lao PDR: Advancing social protection and labour rights and entitlements in the coffee and tea sectors ofLao PDR (SOLAR)” is a new project financed by the European Union from 15 November 2021 to 14 August 2024 that aims to promote labour rights and improve access to social protection and occupational safety and health for coffee and tea sectors workers in Bolaven Plateau, Lao PDR. The project has two specific objectives:
1. Specific objective 1: Extended and improved social protection and occupational safety and health (OSH) delivery system and services at district level in the coffee and tea sectors, particularly for informal workers and women. 2. Specific objective 2: Workers in the coffee and tea sectors, particularly informal workers and women, in three contiguous districts of the Bolaven Plateau of Lao PDR are organized and empowered to promote and protect their labour rights.
The SOLAR project works in three contiguous districts of the Bolaven Plateau region of southern Lao PDR; Paksong in Champasak Province, Thateng in Sekong Province, and Lao Ngam in Salavan Province. The project’s direct beneficiaries are 400 women and men working in the coffee and tea sectors in Bolaven Plateau. They are mostly engaged in informal and vulnerable employment often unpaid and seasonal without proper employment contracts and social security coverage, and can be subject to labour rights and OSH violations as well as violence and sexual harassment in the workplace and households. Some of the workers work fluidly, by shifting between tea and coffee production on a seasonal basis.
The project’s target groups include at least 3 civil society organizations; at least 50 community leaders; the private sector including the Lao National Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Lao Coffee Association, Tea Association, small and medium enterprises, cooperatives, farmer and producer groups, plantations, and processing plants; the Lao Federation of Trade Unions; Lao Social Security Organization and its provincial and district offices; and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and its provincial departments and district offices.
To ensure a strong gender component, MHP will receive financial support tothird parties to conduct a power mapping in the tea and coffee sectors in the target districts (A.2.1.2), and will be in charge of all activities under Output 2.3, including a gender analysis (A.2.3.1), trainings on leadership and capacity to organise adopting GALS methodology (A.2.3.2), and awareness-raising among communities on gender socio-norms and roles (A.2.3.3). MHP will also contribute significantly to the formulation of gender-responsive policy and institutional development recommendations (A.1.2.1). All gender-specific components ofthe Action were designed together with MHP.
MHP will support LFTU, PTSE and ASDSP on gender mainstreaming by using the GALS methodology, conduct power mapping and gender analysis for target groups, strengthen women’s leadership in worker groups including awareness raising on gender social norms and roles, and contribute to the formulation of gender transformative policy and institutional development recommendations.

participating-org.narrative:
the mission statement of MHP, MHP seeks to build the capacity of the people, and poor women in rural areas in particular, so that they have a higher quality of life, in which they can take control of their destiny in sustainable ways. This includes theproper management of non-timber forest products which can be used to improve income and ensure food security and nutrition for mothers and children. At the same time, there is a need to create awareness of gender issues, children’s and women’s rights andprotection of the local environment. Finally, MHP aspires to build the capacity of government staff associated with development work in Bokeo, as well as being part of a learning network for the northern provinces of Laos or throughout the country.
Maeying Huamjai Phattana (translated as women mobilising for development) or MHP, is a new non profit association (or NPA) organisation which has been formed under the recently passed decree on associations (dated April 29th 2009) .
MHP was founded inMarch 2010, when it received approval to form a steering committee for the purposes of seeking registration as an NPA from the Bokeo provincial government. It received official approval as a licensed NPA on 9th July 2010. Its Director, Ms Vansy Senyavong,was previously employed by VECO, while four of VECO’s expected to become MHP staff by the end of 2010. Although there will be some continuity in some areas of the VECO program, it should be recognised that MHP is an independent Lao organisation with a new agenda.
VECO is a Belgian INGO that seeks to improve the livelihoods of family farmers through sustainable agriculture chain development. It started work in Laos in 2002, with food securityprograms in Meung and Paktha districts, and in 2007 startedvalue chain development activities with local farmer organisations in Houayxay, Tonpheung, Paktha and Meung districts. For more information, see www.vredeseilanden.be
MHP takes women, and especially rural and ethnic women, as the starting point. TheMHP team felt that women needed to be given special priority if Bokeo is to develop its development potential. This position was reinforced during the development of the mission and goals of MHP, during which experience was exchanged with other successfully operating NPA’s in Lao PDR, and with Gender Development Group (GDG) and Normai in particular.
